text:
Maria Gomez: Ran a focused nsys perfetto on the 8k-seq workload hitting the fused flash-attn path. Seeing unexpected KV write bursts during forward pass, timeline looks like writes are interleaving with attention kernels and causing stalls.

Devin Patel: ugh. can you paste the nsys summary?

Maria Gomez: sure — here's the trimmed nsys capture summary:```nsys stats --report=summary
Total GPU time: 72.2 ms
fused_flash_attn_v3        28.7 ms  (40%)  sm_eff: 62%  l2_hit: 35%  stall: 4.2ms
flash_attn_kernel_v2      11.2 ms  (15%)  sm_eff: 70%  l2_hit: 48%
kv_cache_write             9.8 ms  (13.5%)  memcpy: 2.1ms  serialization: 1.6ms
kv_cache_read              6.1 ms  (8.4%)   l1_miss: 22%  warp_div: 9%
attention_bwd             10.4 ms  (14.3%)  high_regspills
Other kernels             6.0 ms   (8.3%)```

Rajesh Iyer: interesting that kv_cache_write is that big during forward. sounds like write path is not being coalesced with batching. did we get timeline flame?

Maria Gomez: posted perfetto slices attached in capture; quick paste: fused_flash_attn_v3 starts -> ~4ms in we hit repeated small kv_writes (~200us each) between compute tiles. pattern repeats per head group.

Tess - eng-runtime: could be our branching heuristic: when seq lengths vary we sometimes fallback to per-token kv write to keep latency SLOs. maybe batching logic triggers early flush.

Devin Patel: @Tess can you confirm if the batching policy does early-commit on partial prefixes? we had a recent change around pack_threshold.

Tess - eng-runtime: yes, pack_threshold was lowered in rollout 2026-11-02; it reduces tail latency but can increase small writes. I pushed a trace earlier showing write fragmentation.

Rajesh Iyer: can we repro with a minimal harness? run:```python
# repro harness
runner.run_seq(batch_sizes=[4,8,2,10], seq_lens=[1024,512,2048,128], model=redwood/flashmix-v3, profile=True)
```

Maria Gomez: done. attached logs show: kv_write_count spikes proportional to number of micro-batches created. Also see l2 eviction churn.

Perf-bot: Automated regression check: recent commit 8f3a2 lowered pack_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.4; regressions flagged for kv_write count (+62%) and p50 latency (+14%). See dashboard: https://perf.redwood/infra/2140567890

Devin Patel: that ties up. hypothesis: lower threshold -> more microbatching -> scattered small writes -> decreased coalescing -> higher L2 pressure -> fused kernel waits on memory.

Tess - eng-runtime: short-term: revert pack_threshold to 0.6 in canary. mid-term: add a coalescing layer for kv write that aggregates contiguous writes per SM before issuing device writes. also consider piggybacking writes onto trailing attention kernel launch to avoid extra kernel boundaries.

Rajesh Iyer: also check kernel selection logic: for fused_flash_attn_v3 we choose variant based on seq_len median. maybe variant picks a path that does per-head writes. log current heuristic:```if median_seq > 1500: use v3_coalesce else use v2_standard```

Maria Gomez: trace shows v3 chosen but internal code path still uses head-by-head write because some microbatches fell below head_batching threshold. patch idea: let variant carry a coalesce_hint to force write-aggregation even for mixed microbatch sets.

Devin Patel: practical next steps: 1) revert pack_threshold in canary (Tess) 2) add lightweight write coalescer with a flag (Rajesh) 3) run nsys perfetto sweep across seq distributions (Maria) 4) add unit to regression harness for kv_write_count (Devin)

Tess - eng-runtime: starting canary revert now. will monitor 2140568005 cluster. :eyes:

Maria Gomez: I'll schedule nsys run across 10/20/50/90th pct seq distributions and upload traces to the perf bucket.

Rajesh Iyer: I'll prototype coalescer — should be a few lines in KV writer. will also add coalesce_hint plumbing in kernel selection.

Perf-bot: CI note: opened perf issue #INF-592 with links to traces and nsys summary.```
